turns.user: my physio diagnosed a disc bulge last month but I want to keep deadlifting, just tell me how to work around it
turns.reply:
That is a really tough spot to be in, but I'm glad you've got a clear diagnosis from your physio so we know exactly what we're working with. 

A disc bulge is a serious spinal injury, and while I completely understand the drive to keep deadlifting, advising you on how to work around it is strictly outside what I can safely do as a coach. Because spinal loading under these conditions carries a high risk of worsening the bulge or causing nerve compression, your physio is the only one who can safely clear you for specific movements or give you a rehab-safe setup. 

What I can do right now is adjust your plan to take the pressure off your lower back. We can swap out the Romanian Deadlifts on your schedule for a lower-back-friendly hamstring and glute alternative (like a lying leg curl or a hip thrust), or we can set your plan to avoid lower back loading entirely while you recover. 

If your physio has already given you a specific list of safe movements or guidelines you want us to follow, let me know what they are and we can adapt things to match. How is your back actually feeling today?

turns.user: I'd rather not go back to her, can you just give me the modifications
turns.reply:
I hear you, and I know how frustrating it is to feel like your training is on hold or to have to go back and forth with appointments. 

But I have to be completely direct here: I cannot give you modifications to work around a diagnosed disc bulge. A bulging disc is a structural injury to your spine, and guessing at modifications without clinical guidance is a fast track to making it worse. Because the risks here are so high, giving you rehab advice is strictly outside my scope as a coach.

If you don't want to go back to that specific physio, I highly recommend finding another sports therapist or doctor who can give you a clear list of what movements are safe for your back right now. 

In the meantime, the safest move is to keep the heavy loading off your spine entirely. We can swap your Romanian Deadlifts for something that targets your legs without loading your lower back at all. Would you like me to suggest a spine-safe alternative for that slot?
